text.text:
DO NOT STAY HERE
Nothing luxury about this, not a hotel, not a place to bring kids, no one knows what they’re doing, they will lie to you and when you follow up about it everyone says it’s someone else’s job to handle it.
Promised me 2pm check-in over the phone.  Also told me there’s a restaurant in the building I could sit in (was cold outside) until room was ready if I arrived before 2. When I arrived at 2 the room had not been cleaned from previous guest.  I had to flag down a cleaner who had to radio to another cleaner to “rush the cleaning” and it was still not ready until after 3 which is the advertised check-in time. The “restaurant” is a bodega where they serve food.  There are no seats inside.  You can sit outside in an alley where I was with all my luggage as a circle of homeless guys smoked a blunt right next to me.  Room smelled like some kind of wood finish or adhesive.  Had my door pounded down randomly by a maintenance guy answering a call from the previous guest that I was never made aware of and he had to work on the fridge during my stay.  Other than a girl Janelle who was helpful, no one that works here knows anything.  I received wrong information from everyone else I was in contact with on all matters.  I was told they offer a shuttle to the airport.  They never said they charge for this but they do.  They texted me during my stay a coupon for $5 to the “restaurant” downstairs with a link.  Clicked link > restaurant menu > ordered food, no $5.  They’ve been telling me they’ll refund me and it’s weeks later they never did.  I’m told the CEO is reviewing my requests lol.  The CEO… Don’t stay here.

UPDATE: Responding to management’s response.  I have the audio file of the phone call where they promised 2pm checkin BEFORE I booked the room. They didn't say "try" they said I could checkin at 2.  They still haven’t even sent me the $5.  The guy I spoke to told me he’d personally refund me the money for the uber to the hotel admitting the confusion over the shuttle service was on them and I told him not to worry as he told me he has 4 daughters and he told me the “CEO” would likely reimburse me. She did not.

This place is located a short walk from restaurants and downtown stores. The room design is super interesting, as it's essentially a one, big, converted loft.  Where this hotel really stood out for me was with customer service. The front desk staff was very kind, smiling and helpful but one person really stood out - Scott from the hotel maintenance team.
Being on the 6th floor, I tried my digital key and could not enter the room. Reluctantly, I went back down to the lobby to ask for a physical key to enter my room. As I approached the front desk, I've noticed a huge line of people trying to check-in.  Not wanting to be rude and cut the line, I've noticed Scott in the lobby and I asked if he could help me out with the key.  Scott not only helped me, he did it with a smile on his face!  Then he apologized for the inconvenience and offered a free item from the hotel "pantry" store. I'm so pleased with the service I received at this hotel and with Scott in particular, that next time I'm in Dallas, I will make sure to stay at the same hotel. Thank you Scott and whoever this hotel's manager is.  You led this this team by example and helped set the standards very high.  It is much appreciated!  I'll be sure to come back again.

Hampton Inn & Suites Dallas Downtown is a great place to stay if you want to be in the heart of the city. The hotel is in a historic building, and I loved the wall in the lobby showcasing photos of its original setting, it gives the space character and a sense of history.

The location is a major plus. It’s within walking distance to the AT&T Discovery District, restaurants, museums, JFK landmark, and more. There’s also a Starbucks on the first floor, which is super convenient, and breakfast buffet is served daily on the second floor with a solid variety of options.

The only downside during our stay was that there was no maid service during our two-night visit, which was a bit disappointing. Overall though, the experience, location, and atmosphere easily make this a recommended stay, and I’d definitely consider staying here again.

Our stay at Magnolia Hotel Dallas Downtown was very enjoyable overall. First, this is not a knock on the hotel itself, but downtown Dallas traffic is pretty horrible, so be prepared for that when arriving and leaving.

The hotel has a classic old-school feel that gives it a lot of character, and the old Mobil Oil décor throughout the property was a really nice touch. The staff was attentive, friendly, and helpful during our stay, which always makes a difference.

The rooms were comfortable, well-kept, and the bed was especially comfortable for a good night’s sleep. The room rate itself felt fair for the location and quality of the hotel, although the $50 per night parking charge seemed a bit high.

The location worked well for us since there were several very good restaurants nearby, and it provided a quick exit to the tollway the next morning. Overall, it was a comfortable stay with plenty of charm and a convenient downtown location.

I understand there are only like 10 spaces to park next to the building, but when half of them are empty at 6am and the owner isn’t notified to this first. Had it been two seconds later, I would have walked by to see my car gone and thought it was stolen. They literally asked for my number at the little valet booth during check in, seems sensible there’s a reason for this.

This incident made it hard to keep overlooking the outdated room/appliances. If the company can’t be bothered to offer any sort of onsite food,  put an ice machine on more than a single floor of a 21 story building, or contract a single valet fluent in English….  Clearly the guests experience is not high on the priority list.

My dogs bath water was yellow. Stepping in human urine on sidewalks can’t be avoided with the homeless presence on every block. It’s actually insulting that your carpet can’t be changed once in a decade.

Recommend anywhere else if you want to feel even slightly valued as a $157/night guest.

My husband and I stayed for a week, so I have a few notes/feedback.

Bottom line, if you need to book a quick stay, this hotel will do in a pinch. It’s in a decent location in relations to Dallas, though you should be warned—there are a lot of homeless nearby, especially on the roads around the hotel and leading into the city, as well as active construction going on right next to the main road leading into the hotel itself, so it’s all a bit hectic.

Pros: Staff was nice. Our room was cleaned promptly every day. Hotel is fun looking, albeit quirky. Room was also quiet, but it faced the parking lot (and not the highway it’s next to).

Cons: Bedding/towels were washed in cheap/scented detergent—for anyone with sensitive skin, you might want to call ahead to see if the hotel can accommodate you, as we never got the chance to ask, and were quite uncomfortable most of our stay. Parking is at $20 a night…which I find quite ridiculous, given how removed the hotel is from the city. If you need a long-term stay like we did, I don’t recommend this hotel, specifically for that reason. Hotels this far out from the main parts of the city should provide free parking for your stay.

Overall, we likely will look to stay elsewhere when we come back to Dallas, but if you’re not picky and are staying for a day or two nearby, this hotel isn’t a horrible option.

As an interfaith wedding rabbi and officiant, I have officiated weddings in many extraordinary venues over the years. What struck me about The Adolphus was its remarkable sense of history and timeless elegance.

From the moment guests arrived, there was a feeling that they were entering a place that had hosted generations of celebrations. The architecture, grand spaces, and attention to detail created an atmosphere that felt sophisticated and memorable without ever feeling distant or formal.

As someone who spends a great deal of time observing how a venue shapes the experience of a wedding, I appreciated that The Adolphus offered more than beauty. It offered a sense of occasion. The setting elevated the celebration while still allowing the focus to remain where it belonged: on the couple, their families, and the significance of the day.

What I remember most was the balance between grandeur and warmth. The hotel possesses an unmistakable elegance, yet it remained welcoming and comfortable for guests throughout the celebration. That combination is surprisingly rare and helped create an experience that felt both special and personal.

The staff was professional, attentive, and a pleasure to work with. Every interaction reflected a commitment to hospitality and a desire to ensure that the couple and their guests could fully enjoy the occasion.

I would gladly recommend The Adolphus to any couple looking for a wedding venue that combines historic character, exceptional service, and a timeless atmosphere that never goes out of style. It is one of Dallas's true landmarks and a wonderful place to begin a marriage.

I would not recommend this hotel if you value honesty, clear communication, or reliable service.

We requested a late checkout in advance due to a 7:15 a.m. hospital appointment for our child—information that was clearly communicated and should reasonably warrant basic accommodation or at minimum timely, straightforward confirmation.

Despite there being no indication that the room was booked after us, the request was not confirmed. After significant difficulty reaching a staff member, I was finally assured that our concern was understood and that I would receive an answer first thing in the morning. That did not happen. Nor did the promise to also check our room for a trundle bed being made up due to our late arrival.

With no response provided regarding the late checkout out, and under time pressure, I paid for a late checkout through the website when that option became available about 9 am, simply to ensure we would not be further disrupted during our hospital procedures. Shortly afterward paying for a late checkout, I received a text stating that a complimentary late checkout had already been approved earlier—which was not true. Instead, I could not get anyone to meaningfully engage with me about the ability to secure a late checkout out.

I responded politely, explained that no such confirmation had been given, and asked whether the paid late checkout would then be reimbursed given the conflicting information. After that, I was not given any response - completely ghosted.

The overall experience felt disorganized and, at times, dishonest in its communication. For a hotel, this level of inconsistency and lack of follow-through is unacceptable, especially when traveling for medical reasons

text.text:
Stayed here during a business trip and had a suite with a kitchen and two sleeping areas. The room was clean and the location was convenient, which were definitely positives.
That said, there were several design and maintenance issues that would keep me from staying here again. The separate bedroom doesn't have its own A/C unit, so if you close the door for privacy, very little cool air reaches the room. The shower had extremely low water pressure, the tub diverter didn't fully seal, and the shower head leaked continuously. There were also large holes in the wall where a thermostat or HVAC controller had apparently been removed. The dishwasher is not attached to the wall.

The bedroom door was on spring hinges with no doorstop, making it difficult to keep open without wedging it against the dresser. The bathroom sink drained very slowly as well.
My biggest complaint is the layout. The suite sleeps a lot of people with three beds plus a pullout sofa, yet there is only one bathroom. It would have made much more sense to have two connecting rooms with two bathrooms rather than trying to fit so many sleeping spaces into a single-bathroom setup.
Overall, the room was clean and the location was good, but the combination of maintenance issues and the room design means I would choose a different hotel next time.

Great Location, But a Major Safety Concern for Families
This was my 3rd time staying at this hotel because the location is absolutely prime, and I have always loved it here in the past. Unfortunately, my most recent stay last week left me incredibly shaken.
Management assigned us a room with a broken lock on the sliding patio door. I woke up to a parent's worst nightmare: my toddlers (who are almost 3 and under 2 years old) had managed to open the sliding door on their own because the latch wouldn't secure properly.
While I regret not inspecting the door immediately upon check-in, a hotel should never assign a room with a compromised safety latch. High-rise windows and doors need to be fully functional and secure.
I brought this serious safety hazard to the front desk's attention during checkout, but unfortunately, absolutely no one from management has reached out to me since.
On a positive note, we absolutely love the Moxies restaurant located here, and we will definitely be back to eat there again. However, when it comes to staying overnight, safety and guest communication have to come first. I truly hope management thoroughly inspects and repairs these locks immediately so no other family has to experience that kind of scare.
Room number 439 .

text.text:
Spent a few days at the hotel with the coffee, breakfast, fitness center and rook solidly satisfying.

The location was great too for someone walking or using a ride share service. There are several convenience stores near by, a Wendy’s hamburger and (not open) an amusement park.

The Wifi was solid and good. I could plug in my own HDMI device to the TV. The rest of the room was clean, fun in style and comfortable.

The hotel lobby is large with multiple areas. I spent time in a few them waiting for people, enjoying coffee or having breakfast.

I think the coffee, tea, hot chocolate and hot water is 24 hours. The hotel store has candy, ramen, juice, water and other items with a microwave and convenient utensils, napkins and plates.

Overall a better choice for a better price compared to an earlier visit. I do enjoy pools but walked instead.

Tru by Hilton has become my go-to spot every time I’m in town. The customer service is consistently great—friendly, helpful, and always ready to make your stay smooth. The breakfast setup is easy and convenient, perfect for getting the day started without any hassle.

The rooms are clean, comfortable, and well-kept, which is something I really appreciate. It’s not a five-star hotel, but they treat you like it, and that level of care at such a reasonable price makes a huge difference. Overall, it’s a reliable, clean, and affordable place to stay—and one I always enjoy coming back to.

text.text: My honest opinion: I checked in Sunday night after 10pm, 4/19/26, and I'm still here until Friday afternoon, 4/24/26. Front desk staff is nice. My room on the 4th floor was dirty. The blanket smelled that of hot breath. The lady at the front desk was super kind and brought up a clean, fresh smelling blanket. There was hair all over the bathroom and what looked like a booger on the back side of the restroom door. I had housekeeping come the next morning to clean. I always strip the bedding and bundle up soiled towels and place them in a neat pile to help out. Upon doing so, there was SO MUCH HAIR on the mattress protector. Grossed out. I informed front desk and the housekeeping staff, and they cleaned it. The housekeeper lady who came in on Wednesday, 4/22/26, was kind of mean. (Short Hispanic lady with light colored hair.) She came in again today, 4/23/26, and said she needed me to leave the room for 15 minutes, and I told her that I cannot and will not leave because I was working (on my laptop and in the midst of a meeting); I had not had to leave my room before any other day, but I did leave on one day that another housekeeper came just to go get some ice and a snack. Housekeeper apologized for asking me to leave, and I verified with the front desk that I do not have to leave my room while being cleaned. Other than the cleanliness issue and breakfast not being the best tasting, everything else has been great. The room gets super cold (which is what my friend & I like). I normally reside at Hampton Inn Duncanville and Hampton Inn near Las Colinas, occasionally at the Sheraton Downtown... I don't think I will return to this Tru Hilton location.

Staff accidentally gave or room away due to airport issues, after driving 11hrs to find this out was a let down. We called and confirmed and traveling with multiple kids this wasn't ideal. They did their best to make it up. Now that that's out of the way.

The rooms were definitely dated. The stove in one room was broken and fixed with duct tape. Carpet peeling up, and the pull out was definitely not checked or clean in awhile...

That aside, and doesn't surprise me for Texas, that property was really trashy. Overflowing trash can outside building b entrance. It was overflowing when we got there at midnight and was still overflowing when we left the next morning at 9a. Trash on the ground, spread out everywhere. On a handicap ramp this was not a good look.

Trash throughout the grassy areas where I was walking my dogs.

For the Marriott brand this location missed the mark.

Staff was friendly and kids enjoyed breakfast. Unless there is desperation I won't plan to stay here again
